summary: Serverless Supabase on Cloudflare Pages with PostgreSQL as the database; front end: React + Vite, React Native.

architecture_rationale.text: Supabase provides the API, auth and data as managed services, so a 1-person team ships without operating servers. Microservices rejected: 1 engineer(s) cannot absorb their operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web: A client-rendered app behind login needs no server rendering. Fit for this project: team.languages includes JavaScript; strong cost, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5. Mobile: Builds Android and iOS apps from one TypeScript/JavaScript codebase. Fit for this project: team.languages includes JavaScript; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to social projects.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: learning curve 3/5 for a beginner team.
Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on priorities.time_to_market (strong time to market, which you rated 5/5).

tradeoffs: Client-rendered: no SEO for public pages.
JS runtime adds memory overhead on very low-end phones.
Some native modules need a development build.

backend.choice: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Realtime + Edge Functions)
backend.justification: One managed Postgres project gives auth, storage, realtime and APIs. Fit for this project: team.languages includes JavaScript; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; native WebSocket/real-time support; a 1-person team ships in 3 weeks without building auth/storage.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on timeline.mvp_weeks (a 1-person team ships in 3 weeks without building auth/storage).
Lower overall fit: learning curve 3/5 for a beginner team.

tradeoffs: Business logic split across RLS policies, SQL and Edge Functions is harder to test.
Free projects pause after a week of inactivity; production needs the Pro plan.
Costs at least $600/month but the budget is $0.
Large scale outgrows a single BaaS project.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: strong cost, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to social projects.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: proprietary API increases lock-in; the chosen option wins on priorities.cost (strong cost, which you rated 5/5).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Free global CDN with unlimited static bandwidth on the free plan. Fit for this project: strong cost, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5.

supporting.justification: Included in the Supabase project; issues JWTs that Postgres RLS policies check.

alternatives.why_not: Separate vendor; user data stored in the US.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default.

alternatives.why_not: Another vendor; Supabase Storage enforces the same RLS rules.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.justification: Included in the Supabase project; pushes chat messages to subscribed clients over WebSockets.
tradeoffs: Channel limits depend on the Supabase/Firebase plan.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (image/file processing) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android and iOS (via APNs) for messages that arrive while the app is closed.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.

supporting.justification: Free Developer plan catches errors in the backend and mobile apps with stack traces. 99.99% needs alerting that wakes someone up.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L4: ~2000000 users, ~80000 peak concurrent, ~16000 req/s at peak, ~20000 GB stored
Supabase Pro ($25/month) for production: free projects pause when idle and include ~1 GB of file storage
Upper bound capped at ~3x the lower bound: components do not all reach their peak tier in the same month
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees and payment-gateway transaction fees

warnings.message: Even the leanest compliant stack costs about $1035-3155/month; the $0 budget cannot cover it. Shown as a reduced-cost stack with the budget relaxed.

99.99% availability allows ~4 minutes of downtime a month. That needs multi-zone (often multi-region) failover and 24x7 on-call, which a beginner team of 1 without DevOps cannot realistically run. The stack uses managed multi-zone services; plan for 99.9% until on-call exists.
3 client platform(s) plus 1 major feature(s) in 3 week(s) with 1 engineer(s) is very tight. Ship one platform first (the stack favours shared code across platforms).
2000000 users with a $0/month budget is not realistic for a dynamic app; expect at least a few hundred dollars a month.
99.99% needs redundant capacity in several zones; $0/month is unlikely to fund it.
